The main challenge in identifying technological products of non-human origin, hereafter alien tech, is in separating the wheat from the chaff. The chaff is not just in the form of natural objects like birds, or familiar human technologies like drones, balloons, airplanes or satellites. It can also be in the form of black projects which represent technologies of the future.

It is well known that the B-2 stealth bombers were confused for Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UFOs) during their early test period. Similarly, if China employs today spy drones with AI capabilities beyond those familiar from commercial markets, those may be confused for mysterious orbs and reported as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) by FBI agents in the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE).

The simplest way out of this possible confusion is to search for manufactured objects which represent a quantum leap in technology, akin to the surprising appearance of a cell phone to the eyes of a cave dweller who is used to sharpening stones. Over the past century our terrestrial technologies evolved in gradual steps, each representing a mild improvement relative to what preceded it, and fully understandable in terms of the progress in humanity’s research and development programs. Our future technologies or black projects can therefore be interpreted in terms of understandable improvements in what we developed so far. However, alien tech is unlikely to be close to what was developed so far on Earth, because humanity only had one century since quantum mechanics was discovered and aliens may have engaged in research and development that extended over thousands, millions or billions of years after the discovery of quantum mechanics. If we find their products near Earth, they must have reached our backyard before we reached theirs. Such an advanced alien tech is likely to be incomprehensible to us at first sight. It would look like miracle technology, doing things well beyond our scientific imagination.

How could we demonstrate the existence of alien tech?

Conclusive evidence must involve digital data collected by scientific instruments that demonstrate beyond a reasonable doubt the existence of a technological object of non-human origin with characteristics that clearly deviate from human-made technologies. The collection of digital data on UAP can be accelerated if we can build a device that is able to repeatedly and consistently summon a UAP of any type to close proximity. Obviously, if the U.S. government or its contracted corporations have a physical sample of UAP technology, its meticulous scientific analysis can easily demonstrate that it is technology of alien (non-human) origin by virtue of its material composition, structural complexity or technological capabilities and functions.

In an interview tonight with Jesse Watters Primetime on Fox News, accessible here, I stated that it is my great privilege to assist the Trump administration in figuring out the nature of UAP. I was tasked by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence to chair the UAP Science Advisory Council in service of the White House, the Pentagon, the Intelligence Community and the FBI.

There are two possible interpretations of technological UAP: either they represent black projects of adversarial nations — in which case they are a serious concern for national security, or they represent alien tech — in which case they represent the biggest discovery ever made in science. By revealing alien tech, the Trump administration could make history, get the Nobel Prize and be remembered for many millennia in the future of humanity. Both of the above possibilities about the nature of UAP are of great interest to all Americans. Scientific-quality data can help us resolve the UAP mystery.

Thanks to President Trump’s directive to declassify UAP data, I find a new mindset within the U.S. government that could potentially lead to a breakthrough. Our action plan has two parts:

(a) Look at the best available data within the U.S. government, including footage, materials or even intact alien spacecraft if David Grusch’s claims are correct. If any of this data indicates conclusively the existence of alien tech, the case is solved. In the spirit of transparency, President Trump will then have the privilege of announcing the news to the American people.

(b) If the available data is inconclusive, we plan to collect new data with better sensors. This research will be done in partnership with the Pentagon. If we find that all technological UAP have a human origin, I would still feel that my time was not wasted because I helped the Pentagon and the Intelligence Community fulfil their mission. This is my duty as an American citizen.

One of the people I met two days ago told me that he recently heard from an official at the highest level in the Pentagon that the U.S. is in possession of alien technology and related biological material. Access to such materials will save time over the interpretation of fuzzy PURSUE videos. If the UAP Science Advisory Council can gain access to these materials, our scientists our scientists could help determine their nature and explore whether any resulting technologies could strengthen American science, innovation, and national security.

Last weekend, I visited Peter Diamandis in Los Angeles and encouraged him to announce an XPRIZE with 10 million dollars awarded to whoever provides conclusive evidence for alien tech. My hope is that the UAP XPRIZE incentive will either accelerate the related scientific search for alien tech or encourage anyone in possession of alien tech to come forward.

Stay tuned!

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Avi Loeb is chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council to the White House, Pentagon, FBI and intelligence agencies, director of the Galileo Project, founding director of Harvard University’s — Black Hole Initiative, former director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, and the former chair of the astronomy department at Harvard University (2011–2020). He is a former member of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology and a former chair of the Board on Physics and Astronomy of the National Academies. He is the bestselling author of “Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth” and a co-author of the textbook “Life in the Cosmos”, both published in 2021. The paperback edition of his new book, titled “Interstellar”, was published in August 2024.
